C.   Jeanne Eiseberg, Contract Planner 
Appeal   of   Planning   Commission’s   approval   of:   MS511 - 25   O’BRIEN   LAND   CO.,   LLC 
(APPLICANT/OWNER): Request for Minor Subdivision (Parcel Map) related to a previously 
approved entitlement for a Land Use Permit (L03 - 11), Hillside Development Permit, Design 
Revie w Permit, Grading Permit and Tree Permit to construct 14 buildings, including 315 
apartments, a clubhouse, leasing office, and related site improvements at 3233 Deer Hill Road 
(APN 232 - 150 - 027). 
Recommendation : Staff recommends that the City Council hold a public hearing and adopt 
Resolution 2026 - 43 upholding the Planning Commission decision approving the parcel map. 
Planning Director Greg Wolff said appearing remotely this evening is Contract Planner Jeanne Eiseberg 
who will present the staff report and Robert Hodil, outside legal counsel acting as the City Attorney for 
this item. 
Contract Planner Jeanne Eisenberg presented an appeal of the Planning Commission’s approval of a minor 
subdivision (parcel map) for the   Terraces of Lafayette   project. The original project was approved in August 
2020 for 315 apartments under APO zoning and analyzed in a CEQA Environmental Impact Report, which 
treated the site as a single consolidated parcel. The current proposal would merge 10 existing parcels   into 
one, with no changes to the approved project design, conditions of approval, or environmental mitigation 
measures. 
Staff also provided an update on permits: the applicant has submitted four building permits, with only the 
initial grading permit issued so far; mass grading, retaining walls, and vertical building permits remain 
pending. 
Public comments were mixed — some supporting the appeal due to concerns about parcel configuration, 
noticing, zoning, and project impacts, while others supported upholding the approval, citing housing 
needs, consistency with the Housing Accountability Act, a nd concerns about delay. 
Staff recommended the Council conduct a de novo hearing and adopt a resolution approving the minor 
subdivision and parcel merger, consistent with prior approvals. 
Councilmember Candell asked what “holds” on the project’s permits mean. 
Mr. Wolff explained that the project is subject to 56 Conditions of Approval (COAs) and CEQA mitigation 
measures tied to its 2020 approval. These conditions require the applicant to meet specific requirements 
before permits can be fully issued or released.
